title: Token Slice Investigator — vision & grooming notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures an early vision and grooming notes for a feature weall "Token Slice Investigator" — a console surface that lets engineers and SREs inspect cost and latency at the token granularity across requests, routes, and model variants. Goal is to produce a minimal, actionable UI that helps teams find high-cost tokens, understand where latency accumulates, and map those traces back to model choices or prompt patterns.

Audience & primary jobs-to-be-done (JTBD):
- Product engineers: identify heavy prompts and optimize prompts/prompt templates to reduce per-request cost.
- Platform / infra engineers: correlate token-level latency with serving nodes, batch sizes, and KV cache hits.
- Support & SRE: debug customer-reported high-latency events and determine whether fallback/routing rules are triggering.

High-level principles (keep UX lean):
- Start with summarizable signals (top 3 causes) not raw token logs.
- Make drill-downs fast: list -> timeline -> token waterfall -> request replay.
- Prioritize actionable recommendations (e.g., "trim trailing boilerplate, enable kv-cache for prefix X").
- Respect privacy: redact PII by default, allow on-demand de-redaction for enterprise with audit logs.

Core views (wireframe notes):
1) Overview row (compact):
   - Date range selector, route selector, model variant filter, SLA toggle (hosted/dedicated/private).
   - Aggregate KPIs: avg tokens/request, median token-latency, 95th token-latency, cost per 1k tokens.
   - Small sparkline + heat indicator if SLA breach frequency > threshold.

2) Slice table (list of token slices):
   - Each row represents a "slice" (e.g., prompt template id, route, or user cohort).
   - Columns: slice name, requests, avg tokens, tokens per-stage (prompt / generation / tool-call), avg latency per token, incremental cost, suggested action (auto-suggested).
   - Row actions: open timeline, pin slice, create alert, export examples.

3) Request timeline pane (expand from slice row):
   - Gantt-style timeline per request: parsing -> prefix-cache -> generation (token-by-token) -> tools / function calls -> post-processing.
   - Hover token to show: token text (redacted), token type (user/system/function), latency ms, cost units, kv-cache hit/miss, model used.
   - Small thumbnails to indicate model-switches or fallbacks in-line.

4) Token waterfall (deep dive):
   - Vertical waterfall where each token is a bar sized by latency; colored by stage/component responsible (runtime kernel, IO, batching wait, quantization overhead).
   - Controls: collapse low-latency tokens, group by token type, show cumulative cost curve.
   - Export: CSV with token index, latency, component tags, inferred cost.

5) Heatmap + scoring (aggregate across requests):
   - X-axis: token position (0..N), Y-axis: token text clusters (top-k frequent tokens or n-gram clusters).
   - Cell color: avg latency or cost. Clicking cell brings up representative request examples.

6) Recommendation & experiment panel:
   - If a slice shows >15% token-level cost from trailing boilerplate, show "Trim trailing boilerplate" suggestion with sample edit and estimated savings.
   - A/B experiment quick generate: e.g., propose new prompt trim and create controlled rollout (link to rollouts surface).

Interactions / microflows: 
- From route page -> "Investigate token slices" button -> pre-filtered slice table for that route.
- Pin a slice -> appears in user's dashboard and can be used to create recurring alerts.
- Timeline replay: play token-level generation at 1x/4x speed to reproduce perceived latency.

Telemetry & backend fields needed (minimal):
- request_id, route, model_variant, token_index, token_text_hash, token_type, token_latency_ms, kernel_component, batching_delay_ms, kv_cache_hit (bool), prompt_template_id, user_cohort_tag, cost_units.
- Note: avoid storing raw token_text by default; only hashed/clustered indices and examples with PII redaction.

Wireframe sketch (text):
- Top toolbar: range / filters / export
- Left column (40%): slice table + quick filters
- Right column (60%): selected slice detail -> timeline (top) -> waterfall (middle) -> recommendations (bottom)

Open questions / tradeoffs: 
- How many tokens per request can we reasonably render? (render first 1024 tokens and sample).
- Privacy: enterprise opt-in for unredacted examples? Add explicit audit trail for de-redactions.
- Backend cost: token-level telemetry at volume could be huge. Need sampling policy + adaptive retention.
- Mapping kernel_component: how to tag quantization vs kernel scheduling vs CPU stalls reliably? Work with serving-runtime to standardize tags.

Early backlog (rough prioritization):
- P0: Slice table + aggregate KPIs + ability to open one request timeline (sampled). (ENG-1182)
- P1: Token waterfall + hover cards + CSV export; basic recommendations engine with heuristics. (ENG-1210)
- P2: Heatmap clustering + slice pinning + alerting integration with console alerts. (ENG-1236)
- P3: Rollout integration with A/B prompt edits + experiment tracking; enterprise de-redaction workflow. (ENG-1301)

Checklist before first demo to PMs: 
- [ ] Backend: schema + sampling policy defined and implemented in serving-runtime.
- [ ] Privacy review sign-off for example retention and redaction defaults.
- [ ] Mock data: synthetic requests that hit identified anti-patterns (boilerplate, long tool outputs).
- [ ] UX frames: static wireframes for the three primary states (healthy slice, noisy slice, outage case).
- [ ] Coordinate with Product Analytics to add relevant dashboard KPIs.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Avoid building a full token debugger in v1. Aim for triage surface that routes to deeper debugging tools (SRE trace pane).
- Potential quick-win: show "top-5 tokens contributing to 50% latency" as a search index card. Could be a small component to unlock early value.
- Consider adding a "Why this token matters" tooltip that ties tokens to cost drivers (batching, kernel, fallback).

Related tickets / follow-ups: 
- ENG-1182: API for sampled token telemetry (owners: Lina + Marco)
- UX-54: initial wireframe comps (owner: Priya)
- SEC-312: privacy checklist and retention policy (owner: security)

Next steps (this week):
- Groom with infra on sampling + tags (Mon 11/11)
- Quick mock in Figma of the two-column layout (Wed 11/13)
- Create skeleton API PR for token telemetry prototyping (ENG-1182 draft)

Appendix: shorthand glossary
- Token slice: grouping by prompt-template, user-cohort, or route that is meaningful to teams.
- KV-cache hit: indicator that a prefix was served from cached KV rather than re-generating tokens.
- Kernel component: a tag assigned by runtime to denote where the token latency spent (e.g., attention, matmul, IO wait).

(End of notes)
